To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Hsp70 is induced by cerebral ischemia, and its overexpression is neuroprotective; Hsp27 is induced by cerebral injury and its overexpression can be neuroprotective, while its inhibition can increase injury; HO-1 is induced by cerebral hemorrhage, and its inhibition can reduce injury.

Hsp70, HO-1, and Hsp27 are induced in the brain following cerebral ischemia, and that these proteins can protect the brain against cerebral ischemia, subarachnoidal hemorrhage, and traumatic brain injury.
Hsp70, the major stress protein in neurons, is induced in the ischemic brain, protects the brain against stroke, and is a promising target for stroke therapy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of Hsp70 and Hsp27 in cerebral ischemia, and HO- 1 in intracranial hemorrhage.
understanding the mechanisms of the neuroprotection provided by heat shock proteins, and the development of new neuroprotective strategies based on this understanding.
the role and potential therapeutic value of the heat shock proteins in the brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Hsp70 is a neuroprotective protein that is induced by cerebral ischemia, and its overexpression protects the brain in animal models.
heat shock proteins have great potential as a class of therapeutic agents for cerebrovascular diseases, and that the most promising candidate is Hsp70.
the Hsp70 and Hsp27 are the most important Hsps to be used in clinical trials for cerebral ischemic stroke and Hsps may be used as a treatment for other neurologic disorders.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Hsp70 and Hsp27 are neuroprotective and that HO-1 is neuroprotective in some models of cerebral ischemia and hemorrhage, but that HO-1 can be harmful in other models of cerebral hemorrhage.
Hsps are a promising class of neuroprotective agents that are ready for clinical trials.
Hsp70 and Hsp27 are neuroprotective and HO-1 has a neuroprotective role in some forms of cerebral ischemia but a harmful role in intracerebal hemorrhage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Hsp70, but not Hsp27, protects the brain against cerebral ischemia and that HO-1 is protective in cerebral ischemia, subarachnoidal hemorrhage, and possibly traumatic brain injury.
Hsp70 and HO-1 are protective in most reported studies of cerebral ischemia and hemorrhage, and Hsp27 is protective following cerebral ischemia.
Hsps have a complex role in cerebral ischemia, and the beneficial effects of Hsp70 are not due to the induction of other Hsps.
